reports.title: Riot Platforms Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Strategic Highlights

desk.headline: Revenue up 1% to $181.4m, small profit beats loss estimate; signs $28bn, 910 MW Corsicana AI lease

other.label: Data center revenue
other.change: first full quarter of 25 MW for AMD

results: Revenue edged up 1% to $181.4m: data center and engineering growth made up for lower bitcoin mining revenue.
Mining revenue fell to $116.0m as the average bitcoin price dropped to $70,855 from $114,361; output rose 16% to 1,637 BTC.
Cost to mine one bitcoin (before miner depreciation) fell to $39,265 from $46,324, helped by $24.7m of power curtailment credits.
Net income was $4.0m ($0.01 per diluted share) versus $104.5m a year ago; adjusted EBITDA was $191.3m.
Sold 20,264 bitcoin this year for about $1.5bn to fund data centers, repaid the $200m Coinbase facility, and raised no equity in 2026.

guidance.summary: No quarterly sales or profit guidance. The company gave a long-range outlook for its signed data center leases: lease revenue ramping to about $2.3bn in 2029, with Corsicana delivered in three phases from September 2027 to July 2028.

items.metric: Average annual NOI, all signed leases

points: New 15-year, 910 MW lease with a frontier AI lab at Corsicana: about $28bn of contract value, or about $54bn with both extensions.
Riot now has 1,151 MW leased and about $38bn of contracted revenue; it expects over $2bn of yearly operating income at full build-out.
Funding to come mainly from non-recourse project debt sized to rent; management does not currently expect to issue equity for announced projects.
CFO pointed to a tighter credit market with higher rates; some Rockdale cost risk stays with Riot where no fixed-price contract applies.
Riot has sold most of its bitcoin and plans to sell what it mines; buybacks possible if shares beat the next project, but none announced.
call.source: Earnings presentation (Exhibit 99.2) and the Motley Fool call transcript
